title: Arithmetic Depth, Minimal Gate Alphabets, and Exact Program-State Resources for Single-Qubit Dyadic Programs
abstract: Resource analyses for quantum programs commonly provide safe upper bounds on qubits, gates, or non-Clifford operations. We study a single-qubit dyadic fragment in which the deepest exact resource layer can instead be inferred exactly. Starting from the normalized-midpoint misty-state syntax, we define dyadic program states and the real cyclotomic tower $K_D=\mathbb Q(2\cos(π/2^D))$. For the projective single-qubit Clifford-cyclotomic tower $\widehat G_D\subseteq SO(3)$, we prove the relative intersection law $\widehat G_D\cap SO(3,K_d)=\widehat G_d$ for $d\le D$. Combining this descent theorem with an arithmetic-closure invariant for adaptive stabilizer processing yields $\mathrm{Fdepth}(U)=\mathrm{Adepth}(U)=\mathrm{Rdepth}(U)$: the smallest real cyclotomic field containing the Bloch matrix of an exactly synthesizable channel, the shallowest dyadic gate alphabet realizing it up to global phase, and the shallowest dyadic program-state layer sufficient for exact stabilizer-assisted implementation coincide. At that common minimum, known fixed-alphabet synthesis gives minimum primitive-rotation count. We package the result as an exact static resource effect and outline a certificate-producing compiler.

bite.hook: New research proves that the 'depth' of quantum programs can be calculated exactly for single-qubit dyadic systems.
tldr: The authors defined a dyadic fragment of quantum programs and linked it to the real cyclotomic tower of fields.
They proved a descent theorem showing that the arithmetic depth, gate depth, and program-state depth are all equivalent.
The result provides a formal method to determine the minimum resources required for exact quantum state synthesis.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum compilers need to know the minimum resources required to run a program. This work provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for optimizing quantum circuits.
bite.eli5: Think of building a complex Lego model. This research figures out the absolute minimum number of steps and specific types of bricks needed to build a perfect replica, ensuring no effort is wasted.
